newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends higher, lead by gasoline.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends higher, lead by gasoline.

text.p: The NYMEX oil complex ended higher Thursday after inventory data showing a steeper-than-expected draw in gasoline stocks sent gasoline prices higher, which in turn boosted crude oil and heating oil, traders said.
"People were concentating on the stats. Iraq seemed almost like a non-event in the market today," said a trader.

The American Petroleum Institute reported Wednesday that gasoline stocks for the week ended August 30 dropped 3.71 million barrels, a higher draw than in previous weeks. October gasoline closed up 1.45 cents to 64.41 cents a gallon.
Analysts said refineries are increasing their output of distillates in anticipation of the winter season, but the API data showed distillate stocks still markedly below a year ago.
October heat closed up 0.82 cents to 65.03 cents a gallon.
"Products lead the way today," a trader said of Thursday's price moves. October crude oil closed up 20 cents to $23.44 a barrel, helped partly by technical strength above $23.00, traders said.
"It held above $23.00 over the last couple of days, and people now feel comfortable with crude above that level," a dealer said.
While traders noted reports of continued clashes between Kurdish rival groups in Iraq, they said more significant events in Iraq would have to occur before oil prices would move on Iraqi news.
"I don't think Iraq was an issue today. The Kurds are fighting, but then again they have always been fighting," said one analyst.

On Sunday the United Nations suspended the Iraqi oil-for food deal following Iraqi military incursions into Kurdish regions in northern Iraq. Iraqi troops have since withdrawn following U.S. missile attacks on Iraq.

In the meantime, traders said gasoline could be in the beginning of a seasonal rally which in past years has occurred at the beginning of August, near the end of summer when gasoline experiences peak demand.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, +1 212-859-1761
